body: Book a boat with 'Lucibello' to swim beside Li Galli, the sirens' islands once owned by Rudolf Nureyev
Buy a bottle of colatura di alici, Cetara's amber descendant of Roman garum, at 'Delfino Battista'
Climb the cathedral steps, then wander the Moorish-arched, palm-shaded 'Chiostro del Paradiso'
Climb the roughly 1,500 stone steps up to 'Nocelle', the car-free hamlet perched above Positano
Climb the stairs up to 'Montepertuso' and find the hole in the mountain that gave the village its name
Descend into the cave-set Benedictine abbey of 'Santa Maria de Olearia' above Maiori
Find the 12th-century bronze doors and mosaic-inlaid pulpit inside the 'Duomo di Ravello'
Follow the cliffside path west of the harbor to swim at quieter 'Fornillo Beach'
Glide into the glowing green water of the sea cave at 'Grotta dello Smeraldo' under the cliffs of Conca dei Marini
Have leather sandals cut and fitted to your feet by a third-generation cobbler at 'Artigianato Rallo'
Hike the 'Sentiero degli Dei' from Bomerano to Nocelle, then drop down the stairs into Positano
Hike the ferny 'Valle delle Ferriere' from Pontone to Amalfi past waterfalls and medieval ironworks ruins
Learn Amalfi Coast home cooking and pick lemons from the terraced garden at 'Mamma Agata' cooking school
Look up at the ceramic-tiled majolica dome of 'Chiesa di San Giovanni Battista' in Vietri sul Mare
Order a Franco's Fizz on the sea-hung terrace an hour before sunset at 'Franco's Bar'
Order the black-and-white fettuccine with seafood at 'Donna Rosa' in Montepertuso
Order the crespolini, pasta crepes rolled with prosciutto and cheese, at 'Trattoria Cumpà Cosimo'
Order the Delizia al Limone in the lemon-tree garden behind the counter at 'La Zagara'
Order the lemon-cream Delizia al Limone at Salvatore De Riso's counter at 'Pasticceria Sal De Riso'
Order the tubetti with squid or lemon risotto steps from the water at 'Trattoria Da Armandino' on Marina di Praia
Order the zuppa saracena, a paella-like seafood stew, at 'Il Ritrovo' in Montepertuso
Photograph the ceramic-shard cone facade of 'Ceramica Artistica Solimene', designed by Paolo Soleri
Ride the free red boat from Positano's harbor to a cove-side table and order mozzarella grilled on lemon leaves at 'Ristorante Da Adolfo'
See the Byzantine Black Madonna icon beneath the majolica-tiled dome of 'Chiesa di Santa Maria Assunta'
Sip a drink at the six-seat onyx bar lit from below inside a sea cave at 'Il Pirata'
Split a sfogliatella Santa Rosa on the cathedral square at 'Pasticceria Andrea Pansa', baking here since 1830
Stand on the flower-fringed terrace at 'Villa Rufolo' that inspired Wagner's magic garden in Parsifal
Step inside the Roman villa buried under Positano by the 79 AD eruption of Vesuvius at 'MAR Positano'
Swim off the pebbles of 'Arienzo Beach', a cove west of Positano reached by steep stairs or water taxi
Take the free shuttle up from Positano for the fixed-price, family-style grilled-meat feast on the terraces of 'La Tagliata'
Taste the Furore Bianco Fiorduva, a white grown on cliffside terraces, at 'Cantine Marisa Cuomo'
Twirl spaghetti dressed with colatura di alici inside a medieval convent at 'Al Convento'
Walk beneath the medieval vaults where Amalfi's Maritime Republic built its galleys at the 'Arsenale della Repubblica'
Walk down to the pebble beach hidden beneath the arched road bridge at 'Fiordo di Furore'
Walk the cypress avenue to the marble-bust-lined Terrace of Infinity at 'Villa Cimbrone'
Walk the stepped 'Sentiero dei Limoni' between Minori and Maiori through terraced lemon groves
Walk the terraced lemon groves and finish with homemade limoncello at 'Amalfi Lemon Experience'
Watch Positano's pastel houses turn gold from the pebbles of 'Spiaggia Grande' in the hour before sunset
Watch water-powered wooden hammers turn rags into handmade Amalfi paper at 'Museo della Carta'
